kjv: he went to an high place
mine: he went off to a bare height
note: Hebrew shefi denotes a bare, treeless hill; it is not the usual word for a cultic "high place" (bamah).

kjv: the number of the fourth [part] of Israel
mine: number the dust cloud of Israel
note: Hebrew rova' is usually "a fourth", but the parallel with "dust of Jacob" and Akkadian turbu'u suggest "dust cloud"; the KJV needs a supplied word to make "fourth part" work.

mine: the horns of a wild ox
note: Hebrew re'em is the wild ox (aurochs); the KJV followed the Septuagint monokeros. To'afot probably means horns or towering strength. Context: wild ox (high confidence). Deut 33:17 speaks of the 'horns' (plural) of a re'em, and Ps 22:22 of the horns of the wild oxen: a two-horned animal.
